# Battlefield Executions
The Commanding Officer, whose authority under this provision is not interchangeable with that of the Acting Commanding Officer or XO, may personally carry out Battlefield Executions against individuals aboard the ship or within the area of operations. This includes friendly personnel, dubbed internal threats within this provision, and external threats, such as insurgents, enemy military personnel, and civilians where legally applicable.
# Conditions for Battlefield Executions For Internal Threats Battlefield Executions on friendly personnel may only be carried out when one or more of the following criteria are met: - A Threat to Your Command: If an individual is credibly attempting to or threatening to undermine your command or attempting to remove you from command through illegal means. - A Threat to Life: An individual poses an immediate and credible threat to the life or physical safety of personnel or other persons. - A Threat to the Ship or Operation: An individual poses an immediate and credible threat to the safety, integrity, or operational capability of the ship, allied forces, or ongoing operation. - Endangerment Through Insubordination: An individual deliberately disobeys or interferes with lawful orders in a manner that places personnel, the unit, or the operation at significant risk. - Capital Offense: An individual has committed a capital offense, is in the presence of the Commanding Officer, and is not in secure custody. - (OOC NOTE: LRP Behavior: Out of character or “meme” references, explicit adult content, or otherwise egregious behavior may warrant a Battlefield Execution) Battlefield Executions do not offer any chance of appeal or alternative punishment, if the Commanding Officer has ordered it, it must be fulfilled.
# Conditions for Battlefield Executions For External Threats
Battlefield Executions on external threats may only be carried out when one or more of the following criteria are met: - Hostile Combatants: Insurgents, enemy military personnel, and civilians who take up arms against allied personnel are classified as hostile combatants. - Hostile Actions: Individuals directly carrying out hostile acts against allied forces, installations, or assets. - A Threat to Life: Individuals posing an immediate and credible threat to the life or physical safety of any person, regardless of affiliation or allegiance. - A Threat to the Ship or Operation: An individual poses an immediate and credible threat to the safety, integrity, or operational capability of the ship, allied forces, or ongoing operation. - (OOC NOTE: LRP Behavior: Out of character or “meme” references, explicit adult content, or otherwise egregious behavior may warrant a Battlefield Execution)
# Remote Execution Authority
The Commanding Officer may authorize subordinate personnel to carry out a Battlefield Execution when they are not physically present or are otherwise unable to carry out the execution themselves. Such authorization must come directly from the Commanding Officer. The Commanding Officer must be fully informed of the circumstances, the individual's identity, and the events leading to the order before granting authorization. Authorization cannot be based solely on assumptions or unverified reports.
After a Battlefield Execution has been performed it is required to make an announcement using the command tablet. The announcement should include the following information: - Person (s) executed - Reason for execution (s) - Any relevant additional information
